hypothesis: Yggdrasil F1B's robust hybrid succeeds because pre-coded edge-to-edge identity equality is available; removing or misaligning only this transition-equality scaffold will reduce accuracy despite frozen learned scalar weights and intact 576-byte native state.
arms: Five frozen arms: exact-binding, hybrid, identity-similarity, hybrid with transition-equality signal zeroed, and hybrid with transition-equality rolled to wrong next-hop index. No retraining/model selection/threshold tuning.
cohort: NEW development-only seeds [39720,39744), graph families 4-7, four counterfactual cut conditions and two questions per graph: 384 graph states, 768 balanced questions, 384 new adversarial aliases. Original F1 and F1B are not rerun.
rubric: CODED_TRANSITION_IDENTITY_REQUIRED_IN_THIS_HYBRID iff frozen hybrid stress accuracy >=0.95, ablated hybrid stress accuracy <=0.75, and frozen minus ablated stress accuracy >=0.20. Otherwise TRANSITION_IDENTITY_DEPENDENCE_UNRESOLVED.
limits: This study removes only programmed edge-to-edge transition identity. Public identifier encoding, query start/end matching, and four-hop traversal remain CODED. Therefore even a clear dependence result is not evidence of learned binding, AGI, RSI or production maturity.
governance: Source F1B pinned, new disjoint development samples, original artifact before verdict, one full pytest regression. No sealed first use, accepted-ref mutation, queue/authority alteration, FORGE R32/R33, CKB/KTRADE/controller/broker/production.
